results.title: Bluedot AI Note Taker Review: How It Works | ParrotNotes
results.content:
Score each meeting on three questions: Would I send this summary as is? Did I have to fix anything? How long did it take from "stop" to "sent"?

Then count where your meetings happen. If four of five were video calls, a computer-first tool like Bluedot likely wins. If most were in a room, on a site or on the road, a phone-first tool will save you more time each week.

## The verdict [...] Bluedot is a computer-first meeting recorder that captures video calls without sending a bot. It runs as a Chrome extension and a desktop app for Mac and Windows, with phone and Apple Watch apps for in-person meetings. Its notes, AI chat and follow-up emails are built for people who spend most of the day on Zoom, Google Meet or Teams.

Choose Bluedot if most of your meetings are video calls, you want video recordings and clips, and your team will pay for seats. [...] That is the question most people bring to the Bluedot AI note taker. Bluedot's whole pitch is "no bots joining your calls", and it delivers on that for video meetings. What's less clear from the homepage is how it records each kind of meeting, what the free plan really covers, and how it handles the meeting that happens in a room.
